body: During a visit to the Santa Rosa Xochiac (SRX) reserve, the brigade members took us along a route where we could hear birds and see a great variety of flowers

body.caption: Google Maps image of the brigade members' meeting point

body: They pointed out that, because the population places little value on the reserve, it has been affected by resource exploitation, fires, and pollution
They also mentioned that, in addition to what we could see and hear, there are more living beings that live there but can't always be seen
Considering the great diversity of the reserve that remains unknown, we looked for a way to share it in order to encourage its conservation
As a team, we discussed creating an educational game, a 3D virtual tour, or an informational website
We chose the informational website for its easy accessibility to the general public and its development feasibility
Based on what we learned in the field, a map was taken as the central point, to give focus to this geographic space
Proposed integrating hiking routes, information about sightings, and notable spots into this map

body.caption: First sketches following the Crazy Eights technique

body: More information about the map and its living beings was obtained through virtual interviews with the brigade members and a literature review
Designed the website using prototypes from low to high fidelity
Structured a clear and functional interface, dividing the sightings by type from the left menu

body.caption: Side navigation menu for filtering living beings on the map and viewing more information by clicking them

body: Organized the information into categories for each living being, allowing exploration from a central menu

body.caption: Pop-up window with categories for a bird
Pop-up window with the lynx's physical description

body: We validated the prototype with academics and researchers who have worked with the brigade members and know the community
